# Reality 3D — Launch catalog

The intended commercial catalog, product by product, with every input in the state it is actually in.

The catalog is administrator-managed (Stage 19.8). This document lists the repository seed products (p-101 to p-103), which remain provisional until individually approved. Products created in the Payload admin are the business's own records: they are assessed in the admin's Launch tab and by `npm run content:verify`, not listed here.

**ENGINEERING COMPLETE ≠ BUSINESS APPROVED ≠ LAUNCH READY.** Technically valid: 3/3. Business-approved: 0/3. Launch-ready: 0/3. CMS parity is a property of a database and is reported by `npm run content:verify`, not here.

## Catalog size

| Launch target | Defined | Approved | Launch-ready | Technically blocking | Gap |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 12 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 12 |

The target comes from the launch policy (Stage 19.6 brief: curated launch catalog, target 12–20 products. PROPOSED — no launch-target decision recorded). No product has been invented to approach it; products are added in the admin only when a business decision exists. Launching with fewer products is possible only by recording an explicit launch-target decision.

Not counted towards the catalog size: a service is made to the customer's geometry.

| Service | Class | Implemented | Pricing model | Pricing | Manufacturing | Lead time |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Custom manufacturing from your model (/custom-print) | CUSTOM_MANUFACTURING_SERVICE | KNOWN — Upload (STL, 3MF, OBJ, STEP), geometry analysis, material/quality/finish configuration, instant quote, cart and order | PROPOSED — CONFIGURABLE | PROPOSED — Quote engine rules demo-2026-01, marked provisional: not approved commercial pricing, and not geometry-based | PROPOSED — The configurator offering; see MANUFACTURING_CAPABILITY.md — no process or material is approved | MISSING — No production lead time has been set. |

## Policies

### Product classes

- **STANDARD_CATALOG_PRODUCT** — a defined part at a fixed catalog price.
- **CONFIGURABLE_PRODUCT** — a defined part whose price depends on customer choices.
- **QUOTE_ONLY_PRODUCT** — no catalog price; requires `priceStatus: quote-only`, price 0, pricing model QUOTE_ONLY.
- **CUSTOM_MANUFACTURING_SERVICE** — the customer's own geometry; a service, never a catalog product.
- A product that is not launch-ready is not a class: it is the computed launch status of any class.

What each class needs before it can be approved (Stage 20):

| Requirement | Standard | Configurable | Quote-only |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Name, slug, category, description | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Target customer and use case | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Technology and material (available capability) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| SKU (unique, well-formed) | Yes | Yes | No |
| Pricing | Approved price (price approval record) | Approved pricing mechanism — not yet possible: the quote engine rules are provisional | No fixed price |
| Configuration (≥ 2 material, colour or quality choices) | No | Yes | No |
| Approved media (photograph or approved render) | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Commercial approval record | Yes | Yes | Yes |
| Product approval record | Yes | Yes | Yes |

### Launch stage

Derived on the server from the launch assessment, the approval status and publication — never selected:

- **NOT READY** — a prerequisite is unmet. The admin's Launch status tab lists each one under the section that fixes it.
- **READY FOR REVIEW** — every prerequisite passes; the product approval can now be recorded.
- **APPROVED** — approved, not yet published.
- **LAUNCH READY** — approved and published: shown and sellable in launch mode.

Featured, Published or an approval status cannot move a product past its stage: approval is refused while a prerequisite fails, and launch mode shows approved products only.

### SKU

- Assigned by Reality 3D and entered in the admin. Never generated.
- 3–32 characters: uppercase letters and digits in groups joined by single hyphens (example shape: `RG-GEAR-024`). The scheme itself is the business's choice.
- Unique across the catalog (database unique index; the import refuses a seed SKU already used by another product).
- Required for standard and configurable products; not for quote-only products.

### Pricing

- **Fixed** prices become commercial only through a price approval record (amount in whole rupees, INR, effective date, reference, approver) whose amount equals the product price. The CMS refuses `priceStatus: approved` otherwise, and the storefront re-checks it on every read.
- Output of the quote engine (`demo-2026-01`) is **PROVISIONAL** and is never promoted to an approved price because it produces a number.
- A price approval not yet in effect authorises nothing.

### Images and renders

- Media status: **MISSING** (no image) → **PROPOSED** (an image is set, its media approval is not recorded) → **APPROVED** (media approval recorded: reference, approver, date). A file existing is not an approval.
- The canonical association is the product's Visual (`public/catalog/<slug>/…`), which carries the media approval. Payload Media has no storage adapter, so uploads are not used; the image file must exist on disk.
- Types: **Photograph** (a real photo of the product) or **Approved render** (generated from the product's own verified model).
- Required visual per product: **REAL_PHOTO** or **APPROVED_RENDER**. Until one exists the product is **NO_IMAGE_YET**.
- An image must be classified as `photo` or `render`; an unclassified image is refused, so placeholder media cannot satisfy the requirement.
- A render must be produced from the product's own verified model, show the actual geometry and be labelled as a render. No render is presented as photography.
- The image kind must match the approved requirement (a REAL_PHOTO requirement is not met by a render).

### Product description standard

1. **What it is** — plain, specific, no marketing superlatives.
2. **Use case** — what it is intended for, matching the approved use case.
3. **Technical information** — only verified facts: dimensions measured from the model, counts from the model or its generator.
4. **Manufacturing information** — only approved capability; unapproved capability is not stated as fact.
5. **Material** — only materials offered for the product.
6. **Limitations** — every known limitation stated (for example, a non-involute tooth form).
7. **Disclaimer** — no part is certified for safety-critical use, and none is implied to be. No tolerance, strength, temperature, certification, weight, lead time or guarantee is stated without approved data; validation rejects copy that does.

### Capability status

- **AVAILABLE** — approved by a Reality 3D business decision (a ledger record with a reference, an approver and a date). The only state that can be selected, quoted, carted, ordered, or used by a publishable product.
- **COMING SOON** — planned, on the roadmap (`src/content/catalog/roadmap.json`), and **not approved**. Shown to customers as a future capability, muted and badged. The quote engine, cart, checkout and order creation refuse it; a product using it cannot be published or launch. A roadmap entry has no approver, no date and no specification — it is not an approval and cannot become one.
- **UNAVAILABLE** — not approved and not planned. Not shown as an option.

Capability status is about what Reality 3D can make. It is separate from Payload draft/published, from product approval, from technical validity and from price approval, which are questions about a product.

Now: available — FDM; PLA, PETG, TPU; Standard finish. Coming soon — SLA; ABS, Resin; Smoothed, Matte finishes. A product on a Coming Soon capability can be drafted in the admin and cannot be published or become launch-ready.

### Homepage featuring

A product is featured only when all hold: approval status APPROVED, published, price APPROVED, approved media, manufacturing capability APPROVED, commercial decisions APPROVED, technically valid, and the featured flag set. `featured` cannot bypass launch readiness.

### Merchandising

- **Featured** and **Recommended** are editorial choices an administrator makes in the admin. Recommended labels a product wherever it is already shown; it does not make an incomplete product visible.
- **No sales-ranking claim** — "Best seller", "Most popular", "#1" — may appear in a label, badge, SEO field or copy. No order data supports one; validation refuses the wording. A ranking, if ever shown, is derived from real orders.

### 3D models

- A product's model is a file under `public/models/` (STL, OBJ or GLB). It is verified on the server with the geometry analyser: a closed, finite mesh (or a structurally valid glTF 2.0 binary) that fits the approved 256 × 256 × 256 mm build volume. A model that fails is reported, and the product is technically blocked.
- Customer-uploaded designs are never catalog models: they stay in private storage with their own ownership rules.
